ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Mary Seacole — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Subsequent annual wellness visit; no new complaints. [S]

Mary Seacole returns for her subsequent annual wellness visit, four weeks after her three-month review, when losartan 25 mg was added to amlodipine. She completed the health risk assessment beforehand. Her home readings average 130/78. She has had no dizziness on standing since chlorthalidone was stopped, no falls and no headaches. She goes to the tai chi class twice a week and to a lunch club on Fridays, walks most days with her cane, and says she speaks to more people than she has for a year. Her knees are better. She has kept liquorice paused, takes ginger tea and uses her own liniment on the right knee and the diclofenac gel on the left. She asked to talk about what she would want if she had a stroke. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 25 minutes, with her consent. She named a close friend of many years as her health care agent; the agent is recorded in the chart and not named here. Having nursed many people at the end of their lives, she said she knows what she would and would not want. She wants full treatment, including emergency stroke treatment, for any illness she could recover from. If a stroke or another illness left her unconscious or unable to know the people around her, with little hope of recovery, she would not want resuscitation, a breathing machine or tube feeding, and would want comfort care in her own rooms if possible, with her friends around her. She asked that her own remedies and massage be allowed for comfort if she wished. A written directive was completed and copied into the chart; it will be reviewed yearly. [S]
